text:
Talia Benson: Kicking off thread for kernel auto-selection v2 design review. Main things we need to lock this week: (1) rule ordering / precedence, (2) determinism guarantees, (3) model-family tagging (esp fine-tunes/variants). Dropping notes here so we don’t lose it in meeting chatter.

Yuki Sato: 👍 I can share current strawman:
- Inputs: model_id (+ declared arch if present), gpu_sku, seq features (prefill_len, decode_len target), maybe scheduler hint later
- Step 1: classify model family
- Step 2: map (family, gpu_sku, seq_bucket) -> candidate kernel set
- Step 3: choose “best” based on ordered rules
- Step 4: fallback hierarchy if missing/denylisted

Yuki Sato: Biggest open q: does rule ordering start from “safety” (known-good) then opt-in faster kernels, or start from “fastest” then apply safety filters?

Hiro Tanaka: +1. My preference: safety filter first, then pick fastest among remaining.
Reason: we already know some kernels are flaky on certain drivers/SKUs, and we don’t want tail spikes because fastest path gets picked and then error/retry.

Noah Patel: Determinism angle: “fastest” needs to be deterministic given the same inputs. If we’re doing any scoring, we need stable tie-breakers.
Also: model-family tagging can’t depend on network calls at request time. Must be from local registry / config snapshot.

Omar El-Sayed: From observability side, we need to emit enough to replay decisions:
- selector_version
- model_id + resolved model_family
- gpu_sku (normalized)
- seq_bucket + raw (prefill_len, decode_target)
- candidate_kernels + chosen_kernel
- reason (e.g. “denylisted”, “missing”, “seq_bucket_long_context”, etc)
But please keep cardinality under control.

Lena Fischer: For seq features: can we start with coarse buckets only? Something like:
- prefill: {<=1k, 1k-4k, 4k-16k, >16k}
- decode: {<=128, 128-512, >512}
We don’t need fancy heuristics for v2 if we can avoid misclassifying long-context.

Sofia Ivanova: Scheduling note: we can pass “workload regime” hints later (observed distribution) but not for first cut. Agree with Lena: keep it coarse initially.

Grace Kim: Model-family tagging: what’s the source of truth? Right now model registry has `architecture` for most curated models, but fine-tunes sometimes come through as “llama” in name only.
If we rely on name parsing, it’ll be brittle.

Isabella Rossi: +1. Also GPU SKU normalization is messy (A100 40GB vs 80GB, MIG profiles, cloud instance names). If selector sees “A100-SXM4-80GB” vs “a100_80g” we need one canonical.

Yuki Sato: Proposal for model-family:
1) If model registry provides architecture tag (e.g., llama, mistral, qwen2, gemma) -> use that.
2) Else fallback to heuristics on config (num_heads, hidden_size, rope type, etc) if available locally.
3) Else fallback to name-based heuristic as last resort + mark `family_confidence=low` and prefer safe baseline kernel.
Thoughts?

Noah Patel: That’s reasonable. Determinism requirement: given same model artifact + runtime build + config snapshot, result must be identical.
So the “heuristics on config” are OK if they are purely local + deterministic.
But we should avoid anything that depends on the order of map iteration or non-stable sorting.

Hiro Tanaka: On rule ordering: let’s be explicit:
- Filter out denylisted kernels first (sku+driver+model family constraints)
- Filter out kernels missing required capabilities (e.g., long-context stability)
- Then pick highest-priority kernel by a static ordered list per (family, sku, seq_bucket)
No dynamic scoring for v2.

Omar El-Sayed: +1000 on “static ordered list.” Easier to explain + debug in incident.
Also telemetry should include “ordered candidates after filtering” so we can see why something didn’t get selected.

Lena Fischer: For long-context: can we add a conservative rule: if prefill > 16k, only select kernels from a “long_context_safe” subset? Even if it’s slower.

Grace Kim: That’s aligned with what we’ve seen. Long prefill tends to be where tail goes crazy.

Yuki Sato: Ok so consensus seems:
- rule-based, not learned scoring
- safety filters first (denylist + capabilities)
- explicit precedence list per key
- long-context bucket is conservative

Sofia Ivanova: One more thing: determinism when multiple keys match. Example: (family=llama, sku=a100) and “generic” fallback. Ensure we pick the most specific rule deterministically.

Noah Patel: Yep. Define specificity order:
1) exact match (family+sku+seq_bucket)
2) family+sku+ANY
3) family+ANY+seq_bucket
4) family+ANY+ANY
5) ANY+sku+ANY
6) global default
And break ties with stable ordering.

Isabella Rossi: For GPU SKU normalization, can we just normalize to a short enum for v2: {H100, A100, L40S, …} and treat memory size variants as the same initially?

Hiro Tanaka: For kernel selection, memory size might matter if we pick kernels that increase workspace. But for v2 initial, we can keep a “sku_class” and optionally include “mem_gb” as a capability check later.
I’d suggest: normalize to (sku_class, mig=false/true) at least.

Omar El-Sayed: Please include “gpu_sku_raw” and “gpu_sku_norm” in debug logs (not necessarily metrics).

Talia Benson: This is good. Can we turn this into action items + owners?

Yuki Sato: Action items draft:
1) Yuki: write down rule ordering + specificity precedence + tie-breakers (design doc section).
2) Noah: define determinism contract + propose deterministic replay test cases.
3) Hiro/Grace: propose initial kernel precedence lists for Llama/Mistral on A100/H100/L40S + identify long-context-safe subset.
4) Isabella: propose GPU SKU normalization scheme (sku_class + mig handling) + examples of raw strings we see.
5) Omar: telemetry fields + sampling recommendation (and what goes to logs vs metrics).
6) Lena/Sofia: seq bucket definitions + default conservative thresholds.

Noah Patel: I’ll also add: selector must be pure function of (model metadata snapshot, gpu_sku_norm, seq features, build version, config). No time-based randomness, no “try fastest then fallback” in a way that changes decision after a failure.
If kernel fails at runtime, that’s separate circuit-breaker logic + should still be deterministic in selection path.

Hiro Tanaka: Agree. If we do runtime fallback on failure, it should be guarded + sticky per process (or behind a gate) and VERY visible.

Grace Kim: +1. We should not silently degrade without telemetry.

Omar El-Sayed: If there’s any failure-driven fallback, we need an explicit event: `kernel_exec_failed` with kernel id + fallback kernel id.
But I’m fine punting this to v2.1; initial v2 can be “selection only” plus denylist.

Talia Benson: Cool. I’ll schedule a 30 min follow-up in 2 days to review the written precedence + determinism plan. Please drop links/notes here as you draft.

Yuki Sato: Will do. I’ll post a doc excerpt tomorrow morning.

Noah Patel: I’ll start a small test plan: same inputs -> same selected kernel across runs/threads; also stable across different hash seeds.

Isabella Rossi: I’ll gather raw SKU strings from logs (A100 variants, MIG, etc) and propose the mapping.

Hiro Tanaka: I’ll sync w/ Grace on which kernels are “safe baseline” per family.

Omar El-Sayed: I’ll draft the telemetry schema. Re: sampling, my default is 1% full payload + 100% for error paths, with aggregated counters always on.

Talia Benson: :thumbsup: Thanks all. Closing loop: decision is rule-based selector with explicit precedence + deterministic tie-breakers; model-family tagging uses registry first, deterministic local heuristics second, name parsing last + low-confidence -> safe baseline.
